lines.say: Out of a hundred million users, your app finds you in milliseconds. Drop the email index, and logins can take seconds.
lines.show: Out of *100 million* users, your app finds you in *milliseconds.* Drop the email index, and logins can take *seconds.*

lines.say: Your users sit in a table, one row each, in no order. Without an index, the database may scan the whole table, row after row. A hundred million rows to read. On every login.
lines.show: Your users sit in a table, *one row each,* in no order. Without an index, the database may scan the *whole table,* row after row. *100 million rows* to read. [On every login.]

lines.say: One line of SQL builds an index: a separate list of one column, like email, kept sorted. Each entry points to its row.
lines.show: One line of SQL builds an [index:] a separate list of one column, like email, kept *sorted.* Each entry *points* to its row.

lines.say: Because it's sorted, this lookup doesn't start at the top. It jumps to the S section, narrows it down in a few hops, and lands on your exact row.
lines.show: Because it's sorted, this lookup doesn't start at the top. It *jumps* to the *S* section, narrows it down in [a few hops,] and lands on your exact row.

lines.say: Like a book's index: find the word, get the page, skip the rest.
lines.show: Like a book's index: find the word, get the page, [skip the rest.]

lines.say: The catch: every index takes space, and makes saving new users a little slower, because each index has to be updated too. So index what you search by, not everything.
lines.show: The catch: every index takes *space,* and makes saving new users a little *slower,* because each index has to be updated too. So index [what you search by,] not everything.

lines.say: Postgres and MySQL already index your primary key, usually the ID. Search by email, or anything else? Make sure it has an index.
lines.show: *Postgres* and *MySQL* already index your *primary key,* usually the ID. Search by email, or anything else? [Make sure it has an index.]
